reconcile.connective: Harmonizers read Chronicles' bare 'Timna' not as a son but as a compressed note of the same woman Genesis names — Eliphaz's concubine and Amalek's mother.

discrepancy.connective: Steve Wells sets Genesis' Timna the concubine (Gen 36:12) against the 'sons of Eliphaz' list that includes Timnah (1 Chr 1:36), pressing the same name as both a woman and a man.

skeptic.name: Steve Wells
skeptic.attribution: Steve Wells, The Skeptic's Annotated Bible (2013)

excerpts.excerpt_text: …it should be observed, that Timna, Ch1 1:36 is not the name of a man, but was the concubine of Eliphaz, the eldest son of Esau, and the mother of Amalek, Gen 36:12 …
excerpts.on_tension_rationale: Directly resolves the gender/relationship conflict by stating Chronicles' 'Timna' is not a son but the same concubine Genesis 36:12 names — the squarest harmonization, naming both passages.

pd_work.resource: John Gill, Exposition of the Entire Bible (1746-63)
pd_work.author: John Gill
pd_work.note: On 1 Chronicles 1:28-36 Gill treats this passage directly, arguing Timna in 1 Chr 1:36 is not a man's name but the concubine of Eliphaz and mother of Amalek of Gen 36:12, citing the Arabic version and Alexandrian Septuagint in support.

link.note: No on-topic live page treating the Timna son-vs-concubine tension was confirmed on an allowlisted domain (gotquestions.org, carm.org, defendinginerrancy.com); link omitted rather than guessed.
